standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial sets and cosk_0
standard_prerequisites.statement: The category of simplicial sets, the constant simplicial set on a set, and the coskeleton cosk_0.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both the constructed simplicial set and the target of the map are described through these (source lines 6369-6377, 6383-6386).

standard_prerequisites.name: The fibre-product simplicial set
standard_prerequisites.statement: The simplicial set associated to a map of sets whose n-simplices are the (n+1)-fold fibre products (the author's example-fibre-products-simplicial-object, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the simplicial set whose triviality is asserted (source line 6374).

standard_prerequisites.name: Trivial Kan fibrations and base change
standard_prerequisites.statement: A surjection of sets gives a trivial Kan fibration cosk_0(A) to cosk_0(B) (the author's lemma-section), and trivial Kan fibrations are stable under base change (the author's lemma-trivial-kan-base-change), both retained as context.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two steps of the proof (source lines 6388-6390).

core_obligations: Exhibit the cartesian square: show that the simplicial set with n-simplices the (n+1)-fold fibre products of A over B is the pullback of cosk_0(A) to cosk_0(B) along B (source lines 6381-6387).
Identify the right vertical arrow as a trivial Kan fibration from the surjectivity of f (source lines 6388-6389).
Conclude by base change: apply stability of trivial Kan fibrations under base change to get the same property for the left vertical arrow (source lines 6389-6390).

proof_roadmap.step: Show the simplicial set fits into a cartesian square over cosk_0(A) to cosk_0(B) and B.
Use surjectivity of f to see the right vertical arrow is a trivial Kan fibration.
Apply base change of trivial Kan fibrations and conclude.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-cosk-minus-one-equivalence at source lines 6367-6378: for a surjection f : A to B, the simplicial set whose n-simplices are the (n+1)-fold fibre products of A over B maps to the constant simplicial set B by a trivial Kan fibration. The proof at source lines 6380-6391 observes that this simplicial set fits into a cartesian square over the square of the constant simplicial sets cosk_0(A) and cosk_0(B), that the right vertical arrow is a trivial Kan fibration because f is surjective, and concludes by base change of trivial Kan fibrations. It is short; the substance is recognising the fibre-product description as a pullback and knowing that trivial Kan fibrations are stable under base change.
